subject: Customer routing guidance for US/EU outage — action items & post-incident requests
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@saasvault.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High 503 rate from EU region — immediate assistance requested

Jordan / Redwood team,

This morning (around 08:55 UTC) our production requests to the EU endpoints started returning 503s and timed-out responses. We've rolled back a code change but the issue persists. Traffic chart attached and a small sample of errors is in saasvault-error-samples.txt (attached). Impact: all EU customers for our service are seeing increased errors and timeouts. US traffic looks unaffected.

Immediate ask: can you (1) confirm if Redwood is seeing a regional network/peering issue or a capacity fallback that would explain 503s, and (2) advise an immediate routing workaround we can apply on our side to restore service for EU tenants (prefer a short-lived reroute to US while you remediate).

We're on standby for a call.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
SaaSVault — Head of Platform
ops@saasvault.com

Attachment: saasvault-error-samples.txt

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@saasvault.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High 503 rate from EU region — immediate assistance requested

Alice — thanks for the report and the sample file. We're seeing elevated 5xx errors and dropped connections for the eu-central-1 peering path; networking is the primary suspect while we confirm host-level health.

Short-term mitigation you can apply right now (non-disruptive, reversible):
- Option A (preferred): Set the header X-Redwood-Region: us-west when you call our API to force US routing for requests originating from your EU tenants. This will route traffic to our US capacity pool immediately and preserve session semantics for stateless requests.
- Option B: Update your DNS routing to point your tenant prefixed host to the us-west endpoint under our traffic-rehome hostnames (we can provide a CNAME if you want).

Checklist I recommend we execute together:
1) You set the X-Redwood-Region header on a small subset (5%) of EU requests as a canary between 09:35-09:50 UTC.
2) We validate token and model compatibility for those requests.
3) If good, scale the override to 100% while we keep working on eu peering recovery.

I've attached a short PDF with the immediate reroute checklist and command examples (redwood-immediate-reroute-checklist.pdf). We'll stand up a call if you prefer.

Jordan Blake
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-immediate-reroute-checklist.pdf

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@saasvault.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:42:30 -0700
Subject: Re: High 503 rate from EU region — immediate assistance requested

Hi Alice — quick note from CS ops: we'll coordinate the rollout and monitor cost/latency impact. A few operational notes:
- Please capture request IDs for failed calls and share a sample (we got the attached file; thank you).
- When you flip the region header for the canary, please set a metric tag on your side ("redwood_reroute_canary=true") so we can filter metrics on our dashboards.
- We'll keep you informed on client authentication/timeout behavior; some long-lived streaming sessions may need reconnect logic during the switch.

Karthik, can you provide a short log extraction process we can give Alice for the next 2 hours?

Monica
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick tech details and steps for extracting logs (internal TL;DR with external-safe instructions):
1) From your environment, collect 20-50 failed request IDs and the exact timestamps (UTC).
2) Upload the list to the shared Drive folder (link below) or paste into the ticket. Do not include PII in the samples.
3) We'll run a KV-cache and network path trace for those times. If you want CLI: curl -H "X-Request-Id: <id>" https://api.redwood.ai/health/trace?id=<id> (we'll accept the list via the folder).

Temporary S3 link with sanitized logs and a readme is available to Redwood ops: postincident-log-access-instructions.txt (attached) — this contains how we will pull logs and redacted examples. We'll follow up in this thread with root-cause as we have it.

Karthik
Engineering (Runtime)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: postincident-log-access-instructions.txt

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@saasvault.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Summary & next steps: reroute applied, post-incident follow-up call scheduled

Alice — summary and next steps following our work yesterday: 
- Action taken: SaaSVault applied the X-Redwood-Region=us-west header (canary 5% -> 100%) between 09:35-09:50 UTC on 2025-07-14. Error rates for EU tenants dropped to baseline when routed to US.
- Current status: EU peering still degraded; engineering is working with our cloud partner on BGP path flaps. We expect a mitigation ETA in 6-12 hours but will confirm.
- Post-incident asks: please share the 20 failed request IDs and any end-to-end traces you have. Karthik referenced the shared Drive link where you can upload encrypted samples.
- Postmortem: Let's schedule a 30-minute post-incident call (Tomorrow 2025-07-16 09:00 UTC or 2025-07-16 15:00 UTC) to walk through root cause and long-term mitigations (multi-region failover plan, cache warming guidance, and any SLA concerns).

Please confirm which postmortem window works for you and that the reroute remains acceptable for your traffic while we pursue the fix. We'll also send a short readout and timeline once we have cloud partner updates.

Thanks again for the quick coordination — apologies for the disruption.

Jordan Blake
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
